summary: Planned maintenance, read-only, drain, migration, failover, reconciling, and resolved windows with exact start/end times and time zones, named blocked write classes, local-safe / publish-later continuity, explicit changed-boundary disclosure, and computed review-before-replay — bound to the operator-surface matrix so dashboards, notices, companion, and support exports share one truth.

windows.title: Scheduled control-plane maintenance
windows.summary: A planned maintenance window for the managed control plane, announced with an exact start, end, and time zone; local editing stays fully available until it begins.
windows.outage_distinction: Named maintenance window with exact start, end, and time zone — not a generic outage; nothing is blocked yet and local work is unaffected.

windows.title: Read-only maintenance window in effect
windows.summary: A read-only window is in effect: managed settings and policy writes are blocked and saved as local drafts that publish when the window ends; the route is unchanged.

blocked_writes.label: Managed settings apply
blocked_writes.local_alternative: Saved as a local draft; queues to publish when the window ends.

blocked_writes.label: Managed policy change
blocked_writes.local_alternative: Captured to the publish-later queue against the same unchanged route.

axes.disclosure: Endpoint unchanged: queued writes replay against the same route when the window ends.

windows.outage_distinction: Named read-only window with exact start, end, and time zone — not a generic outage; local editing, save, and search continue and blocked writes queue rather than fail.

windows.title: Drain window before maintenance
windows.summary: A drain window is in effect: in-flight managed work finishes while new managed applies queue to publish later; the route is unchanged.

blocked_writes.label: Managed settings apply
blocked_writes.local_alternative: New applies queue to publish when the drain completes; in-flight work finishes.

axes.disclosure: Endpoint unchanged across the drain: queued applies replay to the same route.

windows.outage_distinction: Named drain window with exact start, end, and time zone — not a generic outage; in-flight work completes and new applies queue.

windows.title: Regional failover in progress
windows.summary: A regional failover is in progress: the serving region and endpoint identity have changed, authority-changing writes are blocked, and queued actions must be reviewed before they replay against the new region.

blocked_writes.label: Authority change
blocked_writes.local_alternative: Refused, not retried: authority-changing actions wait for the new region to be reviewed.

blocked_writes.label: Managed settings apply
blocked_writes.local_alternative: Held as a local draft; replays only after the new region is reviewed.

blocked_writes.label: Provider mutation
blocked_writes.local_alternative: Queued to publish later against the reviewed endpoint.

axes.disclosure: Region changed: traffic moved from the primary to the standby failover region.
Endpoint identity changed to the standby region's endpoint.

replay_review.reconcile_action: Review queued managed writes against the new standby region before replaying them.

windows.outage_distinction: Named regional failover with exact start, estimated end, and time zone, and an explicit changed region and endpoint — not a generic outage implying an unchanged route.

windows.title: Tenant migration in progress
windows.summary: A tenant migration is in progress: the serving tenant, data residency, and key ownership have changed, so authority and policy writes are blocked and queued actions must be reviewed before replay against the new tenant.

blocked_writes.label: Authority change
blocked_writes.local_alternative: Refused, not retried: waits for the new tenant and key posture to be reviewed.

blocked_writes.label: Managed policy change
blocked_writes.local_alternative: Held as a local draft; replays only after the new tenant is reviewed.

blocked_writes.label: Managed settings apply
blocked_writes.local_alternative: Queued to publish later against the reviewed tenant.

axes.disclosure: Tenant changed: the serving tenant moved to the migration target.
Residency changed: data now resides in the target region's residency zone.
Key ownership changed to the target tenant's signing authority.

replay_review.reconcile_action: Review queued managed writes against the new tenant, residency, and key posture before replaying them.

windows.outage_distinction: Named tenant migration with exact start, estimated end, and time zone, and an explicit changed tenant, residency, and key posture — not a generic outage implying an unchanged route.

windows.title: Reconciling after regional failover
windows.summary: The failover has settled on the standby region and the system is reconciling; the changed region and endpoint stay disclosed and queued actions are reviewed before they replay.

blocked_writes.label: Authority change
blocked_writes.local_alternative: Held until reconciliation completes and the new region is confirmed.

blocked_writes.label: Managed settings apply
blocked_writes.local_alternative: Queued to publish later once the queue is reviewed against the new region.

axes.disclosure: Region settled on the standby failover region.
Endpoint identity is the standby region's endpoint.

replay_review.reconcile_action: Reconcile the queued writes against the new region before replay completes.

windows.outage_distinction: Named reconciliation phase with exact start, estimated end, and time zone, and the changed region still disclosed — not a generic outage implying recovery to the original route.

windows.title: Maintenance window resolved
windows.summary: The planned maintenance window has ended and normal operation has resumed against the unchanged route; managed writes are live again and nothing is queued for review.

axes.disclosure: Endpoint unchanged: operation resumed against the original route.

windows.outage_distinction: Named resolved maintenance window with the exact completed start and end and the unchanged route restated — not a silent recovery.

invariants.statement: Every window binds the operator-surface matrix family its kind selects — planned maintenance binds the maintenance notice; failover and migration bind the failover notice — by that matrix's own surface id.
Every window resolves to a canonical aureline:// object and opens that same object on detail, so a notice points at the same underlying object the service-health and incident surfaces use.
Every window names an exact start and end timestamp with an explicit UTC offset, an IANA time zone, and timestamps that agree with the stated offset — never a vague relative time.
Every window names the moment its state was last refreshed and that refresh's freshness, so a stale window is not presented as a live one.

Every window's effective state is the computed no-silent-green downgrade of its phase's matrix state and its latest-refresh freshness, so a resolved-but-unconfirmed window never reads as a confirmed clear.
Every window that blocks managed writes names at least one blocked write class and, for each, the local-safe alternative that preserves the operator's work.
Every window names at least one local-safe action that stays available during it, so a window never reads as a total outage.
Every window that blocks managed writes offers publish-later / draft capture and a write posture that preserves the work, so blocked writes are queued rather than lost.

Every failover or migration window discloses at least one boundary axis, sets its recheck flag from those axes, and restates any changed or unknown axis explicitly rather than implying an unchanged route.

Every window's review-before-replay requirement is the computed rule — required exactly when queued actions would cross a changed or unknown boundary — and a required review names a trigger and a reconcile action.
Every window is marked distinguishable from a generic outage and carries a non-empty sentence naming why it is a known operational window, not random breakage.
The set exercises every operational phase: scheduled, read-only, drain, migration, failover, reconciling, and resolved.
The set exercises both the maintenance notice and the failover notice matrix surfaces.
Window ids are unique, so a consumer can resolve a window by a stable id.
